No Advantage vs Free White Noise App. White Noise Pro

If there is a difference between the Lite and Pro apps. I can’t find it. Save your money until there are additional features.

My doctor has prescribed a med with interrupted sleep as a side effect. I downloaded White Noise to help “lullaby” me back to sleep in the middle of the night. It plays through my Bluetooth enabled hearing aids. It helps some, certainly better than silence.

The app does have it’s issues:

The option menus are not very intuitive, and they are confusing
There are a few “tips” but no manual or help function

The volume of the sounds vary a lot perceptually from one another. It’s just about impossible to create a playlist that does not have jarring volume changes. The app really needs the ability to adjust the volume of playlist entries individually.
There is a shuffle function that reorders the playlist but no capacity for creating a specific desired order by moving items up or down manually.

reviews.text:
Not the flashiest, but great value. Before finding White Noise Pro, I was using the free version of a competing app that operated on a subscription-based model. I wanted brown noise, though, and I wasn’t about to fork over $30 per year for it. 

Enter White Noise Pro. Now I can generate my own brown noise and clip the top end off of the frequency range if I want. The real killer feature here though is the ability to download tons of new sounds. By mixing Brown Noise with one I downloaded called Starship Drone and one of the various rains plus whatever relaxing music I’m in the mood for (Building Game Nightfall Piano is fabulous) on good headphones I can allllllmost completely drown out my boyfriend yelling at his Xbox friends while they kill things. I find myself not wanting to take the headphones off when they’re done playing, though, which may not be the best thing for our communication/relationship, but it’s doing amazing things for my stress level. 

I really wish it was possible to rename generated sounds and mixes. The issue with the mixes is you can’t control what sound comes first in the mix’s name, and if there are a couple of sounds in there with longish names you can’t see what’s in the mix without hitting the little i to see more info about it. The UI isn’t the snazziest one out there for apps of this type, (the mixer pad is excellent, however, really slick) and at times I find it mildly counterintuitive. I’m also not sure why a separate app is strictly necessary to be able to download additional sounds. Oh, I also really wish the alarm clock function had a “shake to snooze” feature. However, these quibbles aren’t even enough to justify knocking off one star because of the excellent value.

Now, TMSOFT, could you find a way to make mixes work on the Alexa skill? And make the noise in the existing skill not time out after a max of 10 hours? Boyfriend and I sleep in sometimes overlapping shifts and 10 hours isn’t always enough to cover both of our “nights” so we’re using a competing product that doesn’t time out.

White Noise's title belies the breadth of sound possibilities available, all recorded very cleanly---I have a lot of experience with sound equipment, and a little added distortion in a recording is physically irritating, and will make it harder to sleep or study (or put the baby to sleep). The "other" noise app (with the owl icon) is also very good, and worth buying, but White Noise, for me, has a better selection of sounds. Regarding the WN recorder: most people don't realize that the iPhone has, I think, the best/ cleanest sound electronics of any phone I've heard, and with a better microphone (iRig Mic up to Apogee Mic), you're carrying a digital sound recorder better than most pro (tens of thousands of dollars) equipment of the 80's & 90's. You can still make great or lousy recordings, but the equipment is really pretty good.
